rationale:
M60 CS3. `exports` was the one relationship type this lane was silent on that C# HAS a construct for: the `public` accessibility modifier on a top-level type. The construct was measured before the rule was written (validation/m14/fixtures/csharp/probe-cs3-exports-construct.ts, instrument B on the parse tree): 275 public top-level types in 400 aspnetcore files, 340 in 400 vbnet-samples files, and ZERO in 300 roslyn files, because dotnet/roslyn is a compiler whose implementation types are 303 of 333 `internal`. That roslyn zero is why this fixture cannot rest on a corpus rule and is pinned instead. Every forbidden row is a real C# shape that must not reach the graph, and one of them (`NestedPublic`) is a REGRESSION row: the first version of the rule read ownerKind === Namespace ? ownerName : global, which accepted a nested public type and published it as a global-scope export, 24 fabricated rows on aspnetcore against 275 real ones — a count that matched a plausible number while the set was wrong. `authoredBeforeAnalyzerRun` is false for this fixture, honestly: the pins were re-derived from the analyzer's own emission after the rule was fixed, which is this lane's stated method and is recorded rather than glossed. The rule is stated in src/ast/real-csharp-analyzer.ts at the `exports` emission site. Runner keys used here are only those script/m14/run-fixtures.ts supports: expectSymbols / expectRelationships / expectSymbolCount / expectRelationshipCount / forbidSymbols / forbidRelationships, with meta.<key> on a relationship constraint. Comment and note keys are documentation and are exempt from matching, which is why each row can state what it convicts. FILE ORDER NOTE: the first version of the fixture placed the global-scope declarations AFTER `namespace Probe.Scoped;`, and a file-scoped namespace covers every declaration that follows it, so the analyzer emitted 10 edges and NONE of them used the `global` source — which read as a dead global-scope branch and was not one. The fixture had never produced a global-scope declaration. The global cases now come first, which is also the only order C# permits.
ROUND-2 CONTRACT CORRECTION (task-37 STEP 3): the export relationship now carries `source: root` and the FULLY-QUALIFIED name (csharp/import-export-edges + csharp/export-arity-collision pin the corrected contract; this fixture was the older bare-name/namespace-source spelling and was updated by measurement, not relaxed). The export PAYLOAD names above were already the assembly-scoped spelling rule and are unchanged.

expectRelationships.comment: positive control: public + top level + block namespace. evidenceClass structural because both halves of the claim are written in the file — the `public` keyword and the name; without the classifyEvidenceTier branch this read usage_contextual, the class calls/uses carry because the BINDING they denote is not written.

the SAME fact spelled the other way C# spells a namespace: `namespace N;` makes the type declarations SIBLINGS of the namespace node, so the owner comes from the file-scoped side variable rather than from a tree ancestor. Both forms must agree.

top-level public with no namespace: no owner symbol exists, so the lane's file-scope source is used — the same source CS-B1 uses for a top-level `calls` edge. `global` is the FILE, not a placeholder; rule R7 bans the literal `unknown`, which appears nowhere.
the other four top-level type kinds plus both record forms, so a fix that narrowed the kind set cannot pass. `record struct` differs from `record` by an unnamed token (see csharp/record-struct-kind).
UNTOUCHED-BY-DESIGN: contains must be unaffected by the new loop

Container is public and top level INSIDE the file-scoped namespace, so it is exported with that namespace as source. It is the tenth edge and was missing from the first pin set, which is why the count said 9 and the run said 10 — the pin was wrong, not the analyzer.

expectRelationshipCount.comment: exactly ten: five global-scope top-level public declarations (PublicAtGlobalScope and the four NOT-exported controls are excluded), one under the block namespace, six under the file-scoped namespace (PublicInFileScopedNamespace, Container, PublicEnum, PublicStruct, PublicInterface, PublicDelegate, PublicRecord, PublicRecordStruct). A rule that also took nested public types, or public members, or internal / no-modifier / file-scoped types exceeds this; a rule that took only class kinds falls short.

forbidRelationships.comment: dotnet/roslyn is 303 of 333 `internal` top-level types and 0 `public`. A rule equating 'top-level type' with 'exported' fabricates 302 edges on that corpus. THIS IS THE ROW CORPUS SHAPE MAKES LOAD-BEARING.
C#'s default accessibility for a top-level type declaration is `internal`. Requiring the literal `public` gets this right without needing a default; requiring 'not private' would not.
`file` is C# 11 file-only visibility; extractVisibility maps it to `private` (CS-B4), which the literal-`public` requirement excludes.

REGRESSION ROW. A nested public type is reached through its outer type, which `contains` already carries, and its export PATH (Container.NestedPublic) is not expressible as a target without inventing a qualified name. The pre-fix rule emitted it with source `global`.
a nested type is judged on its OWN modifier, not on its container's
a public member of an internal type is not on the assembly's surface. Convicts a rule that reads member modifiers without asking who owns them.

public MEMBERS are not exports. The R3 population (every public type AND every public member) was counted at 1,986 edges on aspnetcore against R1's 275 and rejected: it is `contains` again with a modifier attached, and member visibility already rides brain_symbol.visibility.

expectSymbols.name: PublicAtGlobalScope
expectSymbols.comment: no ownerName and no ownerKind, which is what the global-scope branch of the rule keys on

expectSymbolCount.name: PublicInBlockNamespace
expectSymbolCount.comment: the new edge runs one loop after `contains` and reuses its owner derivation and its name-bearing line, so `contains` must be untouched by the addition
